sentences.text:
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 4125 of 2024
Applicant :- Narendra Kumar

Opposite Party :- State Of Up And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Mukul Yadav,Rajesh Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Manoj Bajaj,J.
Applicant- accused has filed this application under Section 482 Code of Criminal Procedure to
challenge the order dated 21.11.2023 passed by Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (Pocso)
Act, court no.3, Bareilly in Case No.160 of 2022, titled State vs. Narendra, under Sections 376(3),
506 I.P.C. and 4 Pocso Act, Police Station- Shishgarh, District Bareilly.

Learned counsel for the accused has submitted that in the trial relating to case crime no.0222 of 2020, the applicant was extended the concession of regular bail by this Court vide order dated 22.10.2021 (Annexure No.2) and ever since then, the accused has been regularly attending the trial proceedings.

He submits that upon registration of case crime no.544 of 2023, under Sections 379,
411, 413, 482, 483 I.P.C., the applicant was arrested, who was released on regular bail on 20.10.2023.

He submits that the applicant was not aware of the date of hearing dated 21.11.2023 fixed in the trial related to case crime no.222 of 2020, therefore, on this sole absence, the trial court proceeded to issue non- bailable warrants against him to secure his presence.

He submits that by Narendra Kumar vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128655692/
1 way of subsequent orders (Annexure No.4), the trial court issued non- bailable warrants to secure his presence and now the case is fixed for 21st February, 2024.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant states that the accused is willing to join the trial proceedings, therefore, the impugned orders issuing non- bailable warrants against him, be quashed.

In response, learned State Counsel has argued that the applicant did not appear before the court on 21.11.2023 and no explanation for his absence was furnished, therefore, the court has rightly passed the impugned order issuing non- bailable warrants against him.
He prays that the application be dismissed.

After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and analyzing the material on record, this Court finds that only on account of the absence of applicant on 21.11.2023, the trial court issued non- bailable warrants and at that stage, not only the prosecution evidence already stood adduced, but even the statement of the applicant under Section 313 Cr.P.C. also stood recorded.
Further, a perusal of the impugned order would also show that neither the concession of bail granted to him has been cancelled nor the bail bonds furnished by the applicant have been forfeited so far, and the court is only issuing non- bailable warrants to secure his presence.
Many a times the accused can be prevented by a sufficient reason to put in appearance before the trial court and every such absence cannot be necessarily construed as wilful or deliberate.

The explanation offered during the course of hearing by the learned counsel for the applicant seems to be probable, therefore, considering the advanced stage of the trial as well as the fact that the applicant is willing to join the trial proceedings, this Court deems it appropriate to exercise the inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
Consequently, it is directed that in case, the applicant appears before the trial court on or before 29th February, 2024, he shall be allowed to join the trial proceedings, and shall remain on the same bail bonds and surety bonds furnished at the time of bail.
Here it is clarified that if, the applicant fails to comply with this order, the application shall be deemed to be dismissed.
With the above observations, the application is disposed of.

Order Date :- 15.2.2024 Raj  Narendra Kumar vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128655692/
